articles.headline: European soccer live updates: Tottenham, Aston Villa both chasing first win
articles.description: Tottenham Hotspur and Aston Villa are looking for their first Premier League win of the season, as another weekend of European soccer begins.
articles.body:
It's another weekend of European soccer and the final one before the international break!

In the Premier League, Saturday's action begins with Tottenham Hotspur and Aston Villa facing off as both teams chase their first win of the season. Later, Brighton & Hove Albion host leaders and defending champions Arsenal in a clash between two teams near the top of the table. Finally, Nottingham Forest host a Coventry City side still searching for their first win and goal of the season.

Elsewhere, AS Roma host Inter Milan in a huge clash between Serie A's current top two. In the Bundesliga, Stuttgart take on Borussia Dortmund, while in LaLiga, Sevilla host league leaders Barcelona.

Enjoy all the updates from Saturday's matches.

articles.headline: MLB playoff picture 2026: Clinching scenarios, bracket, schedule
articles.description: From current playoff matchups to league races to the postseason schedule, we have everything you need to know.
articles.body:
During the final stretch of the MLB regular season, some teams are already thinking about October while others are locked in tight pennant races. 

The Tampa Bay Rays, Milwaukee Brewers, Los Angeles Dodgers, New York Yankees and Atlanta Braves all have clinched postseason spots. The Braves secured a spot on Friday with a win over the Astros.

The Boston Red Sox and Chicago Cubs are also on their ways to securing playoff spots in the coming days.

Beyond those top teams, there are many storylines to watch down the stretch: Where do current playoff matchups stand? Which games should you be watching each day leading up to October? Who will clinch next? And what does the playoff schedule look like?

Here's everything you need to know for the homestretch.

The Cubs, Red Sox and Phillies all could clinch spots this weekend.

Breaking down the AL race

The Rays and Yankees are battling for the AL East crown with the Red Sox also very likely to be playing in October. The Chicago White Sox and Cleveland Guardians are in a tight race for the AL Central title, and the Houston Astros and Texas Rangers are part of a muddled AL West and wild-card picture.

The Brewers and Dodgers have both clinched their divisions, while the Braves also have a comfortable division lead, so any NL intrigue will likely come in the wild-card races. The Cubs and Philadelphia Phillies have separated themselves there, with the San Diego Padres and Arizona Diamondbacks battling for the other spot.

articles.description: Noni Madueke could leave for one of Arsenal's Premier League rivals in January in a search for more playing time. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.headlineJa: 移籍の噂・ニュース：アーセナルのマドゥエケにプレミアリーグのライバルクラブが関心
articles.descriptionJa: ノニ・マドゥエケは、より多くの出場時間を求めて1月にアーセナルのプレミアリーグにおけるライバルクラブへ移籍する可能性がある。移籍情報を扱う『Transfer Talk』が最新情報をお伝えする。
articles.body:
Noni Madueke could leave for one of Arsenal's Premier League rivals in January, while AZ Alkmaar midfielder Kees Smit is on Liverpool's radar. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Several unnamed Premier League sides are monitoring the future of Noni Madueke as a January exit from Arsenal could be on the cards, according to Football Insider. The England international could leave the Emirates Stadium if the Gunners are open to it, as he is struggling for minutes in the early weeks of the season. Madueke, 24, only moved to Arsenal last summer from Chelsea, since when he has scored nine goals and registered four assists in 48 appearances. However, with youngster Max Dowman adding to the competition in his position on the right flank, another move could be on the cards.

- Liverpool are among a whole host of teams tracking AZ Alkmaar midfielder Kees Smit, TEAMtalk reports. The 20-year-old has been a regular for the Dutch side over the past two seasons, with this campaign offering him a chance to impress in the Eredivisie and the Europa League once again. Liverpool are long-term admirers of Smit, who made his senior debut for Netherlands in March but did not make the cut for their 2026 FIFA World Cup squad.

- Arsenal are following the progress of Sturm Graz youngster Luca Weinhandl, along with fellow Premier League clubs Aston Villa and Brighton & Hove Albion, according to TEAMtalk. The 17-year-old made his breakthrough last season with 10 appearances in the Austrian Bundesliga. This season he has already seen him feature five times, along with a start in the Europa League. A £20 million package could reportedly be enough to land Weinhandl, as teams position themselves for the January transfer window.

- New York City FC is closing in on the signing of defender Matt Miazga as a free agent, days after FC Cincinnati waived his contract, The Athletic reports. The 31-year-old is closing in on the switch with NYCFC aiming for a place in this season's playoffs. Miazga, who has won 28 caps for the USMNT, has plenty of experience in MLS, and was named the MLS Defender of the Year in 2023. After 108 appearances with Cincinnati, the former Chelsea man will now be looking to make an impact with NYCFC.

- Juventus are preparing talks with Nicolás González over a contract extension during the upcoming international break. Nicolo Schira states that the winger could sign for an extra year or two, with his current deal running until 2029. González spent last season on loan at Atlético Madrid, and while an approach was made for the 28-year-old by the Rojiblancos, as well as Inter Milan and a Saudi Pro League team, he decided to stay at the club. The forward has two goals and one assist to his name in four appearances since returning to Turin, as he looks to consolidate that form with a new contract.

articles.headline: Sources: Pistons, Ausar Thompson reach 5-year, $155M extension
articles.description: Pistons All-Defensive forward Ausar Thompson has agreed to a five-year, $155 million rookie-scale contract extension, sources told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者：ピストンズとアサー・トンプソンが5年1億5500万ドルの延長契約に合意
articles.descriptionJa: ピストンズのオールディフェンシブチーム選出フォワード、アサー・トンプソンが5年1億5500万ドルのルーキースケール延長契約に合意したと、関係者がESPNに明かしました。
articles.body:
Detroit Pistons forward Ausar Thompson has agreed to a five-year, $155 million rookie-scale contract extension with the franchise, sources told ESPN on Friday.

Thompson lands the fully guaranteed extension after making first-team All-Defense and finishing third in Defensive Player of the Year voting last season. The 23-year-old averaged 9.9 points, 5.7 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 0.9 blocks in 2025-26 while leading the NBA in steals per game (2.0).

He had the third-most combined steals and blocks last season at 215 and is one of three players with at least 300 steals and 150 blocks since entering the NBA as the No. 5 pick in the 2023 draft.

In 14 playoff games during Detroit's run to the Eastern Conference semifinals, Thompson averaged 8.2 points, 7.9 rebounds, 3.1 assists, 2 steals and 1.8 blocks, becoming the first player with at least 25 steals and 25 blocks in a postseason since Anthony Davis in 2020.

Thompson and his twin, Amen Thompson of the Houston Rockets, are now the first brothers to each receive a $100 million NBA deal. Amen Thompson signed a five-year, $208 million rookie extension with the Rockets recently, giving both a combined $363 million this offseason.

Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon has held concurrent negotiations with two priority players in restricted free agent Jalen Duren and Thompson. The Pistons have remained engaged in talks with Duren since June, offering a contract in the range of more than $190 million. Thus far the sides have been dug in, with Detroit believing it has made fair offers and Duren wanting more.

Thompson's sophomore season was cut short when he was diagnosed with a blood clot in March 2024. Eight months later, Thompson was cleared by the NBA's fitness-to-play panel and successfully returned to action.

ESPN Research contributed to this report.

articles.headline: NFL Week 2 predictions: Upsets, fantasy sleepers, stat lines
articles.description: Will Ashton Jeanty pile up the scrimmage yards? Could the Bengals upset the Texans? And can George Pickens find the end zone?
articles.body:
Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season is off to an exciting start, as the Bills defeated the Lions 41-31 in the first game at Highmark Stadium. But what will happen in the remaining 15 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs who could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projected out stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody gives three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen suggests three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

Could the Bengals upset the Texans? Will we see big receiving days for the Dolphins' Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas? Can Eagles running back Saquon Barkley find the end zone? And is it finally time for the Jets to snag an interception? Let's make 15 big predictions for all of Sunday and Monday's action.

Jump to:

Upset picks | Projected stat lines

Fantasy sleepers, surprises

TD scorers | Other predictions

Maldonado predicts two upsets

Jacksonville Jaguars +2.5 at Denver Broncos (+124)

Denver's offense hasn't shown enough to justify laying points. The Broncos produced only 176 yards and 3.7 yards per play in their Week 1 loss to the Chiefs, with quarterback Bo Nix turning it over twice. Jacksonville is bringing a pass rush that generated five sacks against Cleveland, while QB Trevor Lawrence threw four touchdown passes. Defense makes the Broncos the favorite, but the Jaguars have the more trustworthy offense to win outright.

Cincinnati Bengals +2.5 at Houston Texans (+120)

The Bengals' biggest weakness looked better against the Bucs, as quarterback Joe Burrow was sacked only once. If that holds, he gets a Houston defense that just allowed 10.4 yards per pass to Buffalo in Week 1. Houston can obviously pressure Burrow, but if Cincinnati's offensive line continues to improve, it should have enough through the air with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.

Walder predicts three stat lines

Rhamondre Stevenson, RB, New England Patriots: 16 carries, 63 rushing yards; 5 receptions, 42 receiving yards, 1 receiving touchdown

Since 2023, running backs catch passes on 8% of dropbacks against man coverage but 15% against zone coverage. Why does that matter here? Because in Week 1 against the Falcons, the Steelers ran zone coverage 89% of the time under new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham. So I expect Stevenson to have a big day in the receiving game.

And while I don't expect the Patriots will be as run-heavy as they were in Week 1 -- which certainly didn't work out for them! -- New England should be ahead by enough early to run the ball late in the game. All in all, it should be a healthy workload for Stevenson.

articles.headline: Who is Commanders' special teams ace Tyler Owens?
articles.description: J.J. Watt called Owens' play against the Eagles 'legitimately one of the greatest football plays I've ever seen.'
articles.body:
ASHBURN, Va. -- The play, viewed more than 18 million times on one social media platform, went like this: Washington Commanders special-teamer Tyler Owens, ready to cover a punt, stepped outside then cut back inside and ripped through a double-team at the line of scrimmage. He flung one blocker to the side then stiff-armed the other as he raced downfield. When the other blocker caught back up to Owens, he shoved him to the ground then did the same to the second one.

Owens looked like a man chasing someone stealing his car.

And then Owens reached the returner, who decided to leap. Bad decision. Owens corralled him and body-slammed him to the ground. Owens then got up and casually walked to the sideline, as if he had just clocked out of work for the day.

"It was just a good rep," he said.

Others begged to differ. Former Pro Bowl defensive end J.J. Watt called it "legitimately one of the greatest football plays I've ever seen." It has been viewed more than 11.6 million times on the NFL's X feed and another 6.9 million times on the NFLmemes feed. More than 40,000 people liked it on the NFL's Instagram page.

"I was just out there playing football," Owens said. "It never really stood out to me until after."

And though it introduced Owens to the sporting world, his teammates needed no introductions. They already knew what he could do -- and has done. They might have been impressed by the play, but they were not surprised.

There's a reason Owens made the Commanders as an undrafted free agent in 2024; he made two plays that summer to stand out. Those plays also prompted coach Dan Quinn to make an unusual announcement in a team meeting about Owens. His special teams coach at Texas Tech, Kenny Perry, could point to plays in college that prompted him to tell Owens he would make a long living in the NFL.

"That's what he's been doing," said Washington safety Jeremy Reaves, a special teams Pro Bowler after the 2022 season. "He's done that over and over and over again. That's who he is."

Commanders punter Tress Way, who has been in the league since 2014, said he gets the same question from coordinators or assistant coaches on other teams.

"Just about every team we play, they're like, 'What do you guys feed 18?'" Way said. "I tell them punt returners."

Three days after the play, after he had become a teaching tool for special teams coaches at every level and after seeing the reaction and appearing on "The Pat McAfee Show," Owens knows it was more than "just a good rep."

And though other plays stand out in his mind, this one vs. the Eagles vaulted to the top.

"I would say this is my favorite," Owens said. "Just because of the physicality. ... It's just rewarding. You put in all this work, finally get to see something come out of it."

What he saw was a viral reaction.

"Just all the GOATS retweeting it and stuff like that. It's pretty dope," Owens said. "I like it."

articles.headline: How the 49ers are readjusting after weeklong Australia trip
articles.description: On their 16-hour flight home from Australia, the 49ers chose sleep over celebration. That kick-started a long week of getting back into routine.
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- After a convincing 27-7 win over a division rival, the San Francisco 49ers boarded their buses and headed to the Melbourne airport with visions of a victory party dancing in their heads.

The Niners knew they couldn't take off before the Los Angeles Rams' departed, but they still had every intention of making the most of the 16-hour flight home. But by the time they boarded the plane, all of those plans stayed on the ground, as adrenaline gave way to the fatigue from their weeklong trip down under.

"We're all like, dude, we're going to fall asleep and then we're going to wake up and we're going to celebrate," fullback Kyle Juszczyk said. "We're going to have our team party that we didn't get to have. And then I woke up like an hour before we got there, and everyone was still sleeping. I don't think anybody celebrated."

While they had every reason to celebrate in the moment, the fact that they didn't should only help them overcome the final obstacle of the Australia trip: reacclimating to Pacific time and a normal workweek.

Asked this week whether it was more difficult to adjust to Australian time or readjusting to Pacific time, there were players on both sides of the fence. But they all agreed there was at least a little bit of an adjustment period.

"Speaking for myself, I felt like crap all weekend," coach Kyle Shanahan said. "We had two days off and I did not feel right. Took a couple of days. I think I was good by Monday. Talking to some of the guys, some guys felt fine right away. Some went through the same stuff, but I think we're definitely all good by now."

Much like they did for the flight to Melbourne, the Niners had recovery plans for their players that began as soon as they stepped back on the Qantas A380 plane. Dustin Perry, the team's vice president of player health and performance, and his staff provided players with instructions on how much water to drink on the plane, how long to stay up before falling asleep and when to wake up.

Right tackle Colton McKivitz said the objective was to stay up for a couple of hours (an easy enough task with so much adrenaline still pumping from the game), go to sleep in their lie-flat seats, and then wake up for the final few hours of the flight.

McKivitz estimated he slept for about seven hours. Running back Christian McCaffrey said he was out for about 13 hours, which was about the same as rookie defensive tackle Gracen Halton. Defensive end Nick Bosa was in the same range.

"I actually felt it worse on the way back," Bosa said. "Going out, you just kind of power through a few hours and then go to bed early and then just stay on a little earlier wake-up is what I did. And then when I came back, it's been kind of hard to get to bed, but [Tuesday] night I got to bed nice and early."
